source_title: The Book of the New Sun
continuity_scope: Pass limited to Gene Wolfe's The Shadow of the Torturer, Simon & Schuster first edition ISBN 9780671253251, Book One only. Excludes the rest of the tetralogy, The Urth of the New Sun coda, related Solar Cycle works, adaptations, and author interviews as story canon.
coverage_rule: Eight named individual dramatic characters in this one novel. Guilds, occupations, archaic vocabulary, creatures, artifacts, places, cosmology, and motifs remain dimensions or terms rather than relationship endpoints.
omissions: The remaining New Sun volumes, the coda, related Solar Cycle fiction, adaptation material, and author interviews as canon.
Collective guilds, creatures, places, artifacts, and narrative devices as character nodes.
uncertainties: Severian narrates retrospectively and presents an unstable account; motive, memory, chronology, and identity claims are retained only as this novel presents them.
The text's archaic or translated-seeming English is treated as source-specific vocabulary, not evidence of a real-language etymology.
Torture, execution, sexual coercion, violence, trauma, and captivity require contextual care; chapter locators avoid pagination variance.
evidence_basis: Primary claims use the declared printed witness and chapter loci. Macmillan's official Shadow & Claw record confirms that it contains The Shadow of the Torturer and credits the novel to Wolfe, but the pass does not draw story claims from its companion novel.

citations.locator: Macmillan Shadow & Claw record, contents statement
supports: Publisher bibliographic confirmation that the omnibus includes The Shadow of the Torturer by Gene Wolfe.
